name: companion-pet-customize
description: companion-pet rarity/species/hat/eyes customization via landmark-based binary patch; may be complex — assess feasibility
archive_reason: The companion-pet/gacha "buddy" feature that this patch targets does not exist in the pristine 2.1.158 binary, so no anchor can be matched. The upstream crack (Pickle-Pixel/claudecode-buddy-crack) flips a spread operator from `return { ...stored, ...bones }` to `return { ...bones, ...stored }`, anchored on the landmark `let{bones:`. None of the load-bearing identifiers from this feature are present in /tmp/ccx-test/claude-pristine: regex searches over the raw bytes returned occurrences==0 for b'bones', b'{bones:', b'inspirationSeed', b'CompanionBones', b'companionUserId', b'...stored', b'...bones', b'rarity', and b'Sprite' (only 1 unrelated 'legendary', 0 'rarity'). The 12 b'companion' hits are all the unrelated event-type string 'companion_intro' (e.g. offsets 202031205, 203676496 inside `new Set(["compaction_reminder","companion_intro","pen_mode_enter","pen_mode_exit"])`) plus Kotlin/Stata keyword-list noise in non-region data (~167M, ~199M). The b'buddy'/b'Buddy' hits are 'onboarding buddy' (205887989) and '/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy' (197155168, 85813634), not the pet feature. The 79 matches of the generic spread pattern `...\w,...\w}` are ordinary minified code, none tied to companion bones. The buddy source under /tmp/cc-2188/buddy/ (companion.ts, sprites.ts, CompanionSprite.tsx) is a separate/third-party feature codebase the crack assumes is compiled in; stock Claude Code 2.1.158 does not ship it. Because the target code is entirely absent, there is no stable unique in-region anchor to patch.
